author_credibility.justification: All authors are affiliated with credible institutions with relevant expertise. The study involves two main institutions: Niigata University and the University of Leicester. However, the corresponding author has a low publication record (2 papers) and h-index (1), which limits their established expertise. There are no commercial affiliations among the main institutions, but there are multiple clinics involved that are primarily healthcare facilities rather than research-focused.
institutions_assessed: University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust

research_question_and_methods.justification: The objectives and hypotheses are explicit, testable, and the methodology is detailed enough to replicate the study. It addresses a significant public health concern regarding influenza outbreaks.
research_question_and_methods.quote: This study aims to investigate the genetic features of the hemagglutinin (HA) genes of influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria viruses circulating in Japan during the 2023–2024 season.

results_and_conclusion.justification: The results are not well-supported and conclusions seem overstated, with inconsistencies in reporting. The absence of statistical analysis adds to the lack of clarity.
results_and_conclusion.quote: No PA/I38T substitutions were detected in any pre-treatment sample.

references.justification: The reference list includes a balanced mix of foundational, recent, and domain-relevant peer-reviewed studies, providing a good context for the work.
